newsitem.title: USA: Magna to buy Homeland in $216 mln deal.
newsitem.headline: Magna to buy Homeland in $216 mln deal.

text.p: Magna Group Inc and Homeland Bankshares Corp said Tuesday they signed a definitive agreement under which Homeland will acquire Magna.
Under the agreement, Magna will issue 5,038,934 shares of Magna common stock and pay $91,966,970 in cash in exchange for all the outstanding Homeland common shares.
Homeland is the second largest bank holding company headquartered in Iowa with total assets of $1.20 billion as of June 30.
Each share of Homeland's common stock may be exchanged for about 1.55 shares of Magna common stock or a comparable amount in cash, the companies said.
Homeland stockholders may elect to receive all Magna common stock, all cash or a mixture of stock and cash, subject to certain limitations, they added.
The transaction has a current aggregate market value of about $216 million.
The acquisition is expected to be completed in the first quarter of 1997.
The deal is subject to regulatory approval, a Homeland shareholder vote and other conditions.
G. Thomas Andes, chairman of Magna, said the acquisition will be accretive to earnings within 12 months.

"Based on our analysis, cost savings of approximately $8 million can be achieved through centralization of systems and procedures, and the consolidation of the various bank charters," Andes said in a statement. "This acquisition opens a whole new market and offers growth and revenue enhancement opportunities for Magna."
Homeland owns and operates four comercial banks and one savings bank and provides financial services through a network of 33 locations in Iowa.
Magna Group, with $5.35 billion in assets, has 106 banking locations throughout Illinois and Missouri and a trust and brokerage company.

After the deal is completed, Erl Schmiesing, chairman and president of Homeland, and Douglas Shull, treasurer and chief financial officer of Casey's General Stores Inc, will become Magna directors. Shull is currently a Homeland director.
